clauses.reason: The only command is: "I hereby exempt the said Hugh H. Bennett from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending April 30, 1952." The order fixes the length of the exemption, so it ended by its own terms with the last day of that period. April 30, 1952 is recorded as the end date on the inclusive reading (the exemption runs through that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends as April 30 begins, is the alternative. No held order revokes or extends the exemption, so this is the first end. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory records this clause as the five characters '1952.'. The operative command is the single sentence that begins 'NOW, THEREFORE' and ends 'April 30, 1952.'; the two WHEREAS paragraphs are recitals (Bennett will become subject to compulsory retirement in April 1951; the public interest requires the exemption) and carry no command.

research_rationale:
EO 10229 (16 FR 2865, Federal Register of Tuesday, April 3, 1951; signed March 30, 1951; F.R. Doc. 51-4006) has one operative command: under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 404; 5 U.S.C. 715a) the President exempts Hugh H. Bennett, Chief of the Soil Conservation Service, from compulsory retirement for age under the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, for a stated period. The order fixes its own term, so the first end is the own-terms end date April 30, 1952. Under the 2026-10-21 until-date ruling it is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of April 30, 1952); the exclusive reading, under which the term ends as April 30 begins, is the alternative. The held Federal Register text confirms identity (number, title, date and document number agree with the census register row). The end is cited to the held Federal Register text of the order itself, a government printed copy (OCR text layer of the official PDF, whose page images were not opened), because the packet registers no own-term record on that text.

savings.reason: The exemption was permission for Bennett to remain in service past the compulsory retirement age during the term; whatever service and pay it allowed before the term ended is accrued. Nothing in the order continues the exemption after the term ends, and the order says nothing about annuity rights, which the Civil Service Retirement Act governs.
